subject: fixed effects in a 4way via scan1coef

messages.author: 04e62c3b36bb17bf
messages.subject: fixed effects in a 4way via scan1coef
parts:
Hi Karl et al,
I am working with a 4-way mapping population where parental genotypes [A,B,C,D] come from two subspecies:
subspecies 1: [A,C]
subspecies 2: [B,D]

which produces four genotypes [AC,BC,AD,BD]:
fixed subspecies 1: [AC]
hybrids: [AD, BC]
fixed subspecies 2: [BD] 

I want to use scan1coef to test three hypotheses with three separate contrasts: 
H0 #1: parent A is the same as parent B, contrast = c(-1,1,-1,1)
H0 #2: parent C is the same as parent D, contrast = c(-1,-1,1,1)
H0 #3: subspecies 1 is the same as subspecies 2, contrast = c(-1,0,0,1)

So, I supply this contrast matrix to scan1coef:

```
contrast.mat <-cbind(
    mu = c(1, 1, 1, 1), 
    add1 = c(-1, 1, -1, 1),
    add2 = c(-1, -1, 1, 1), 
    fixed = c(-1, 0, 0, 1))
```

However, this matrix produces NAs for the fixed contrast. Is the issue the way that I am setting up the contrast matrix, or simply that I can't make this type of test simultaneously?

Any help is much appreciated.
Thanks,
John







Here is the code to replicate the issue:

```
data(fake.4way)
contrast.mat <-cbind(
  mu = c(1, 1, 1, 1), 
  add1 = c(-1, 1, -1, 1),
  add2 = c(-1, -1, 1, 1), 
  fixed = c(-1, 0, 0, 1))
sex.matrix <- as.matrix(fake.4way$pheno[,"sex"])
pheno.mat <- as.matrix(fake.4way$pheno[,"phenotype"])

probs <- qtl2convert::probs_qtl_to_qtl2(
  calc.genoprob(
    subset(fake.4way, chr = 1), 
    step = 0))$probs
rownames(pheno.mat) <- rownames(sex.matrix) <- 1:nind(fake.4way)

s1coef.out <- scan1coef(
  genoprobs = probs, 
  pheno = pheno.mat,
  kinship = NULL, 
  addcovar = sex.matrix, 
  intcovar = sex.matrix, 
  se = TRUE,
  contrasts = contrast.mat)
```

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl2-disc] fixed effects in a 4way via scan1coef
parts:
The contrast matrix needs to be full-rank.

  Matrix::rankMatrix(contrast.mat) # gives 3

You could change the 4th column to (1, -1, -1, 1)

  contrast.mat[,4] <- c(1, -1, -1, 1)
  Matrix::rankMatrix(contrast.mat) # now gives 4

karl

OK - that makes sense. Figured it had to be full rank. 

My last goal is to test if there is a difference between the AC and BD genotypes, ignoring the AD and BC genotypes. So, I can't make that test in the same contrast matrix as the cross-specific tests. 
Would it be appropriate to construct a different full-rank contrast matrix and just extract the test of interest out of that?

contrast.mat <-cbind(
    mu = c(1, 1, 1, 1),

not1 = c(-1, 0, 0, -1),
    not2 = c(0, 0, -1, 1), 
    fixed = c(-1, 0, 0, 1)) # this one for the fixed differences between subspecies.

Thanks!
John
